facts.statement: Coringasuchus is a genus of mesoeucrocodylian crocodyliform that is possibly classified as a notosuchian.
facts.quote: Coringasuchus is a genus of mesoeucrocodylian crocodyliform, perhaps a notosuchian.

facts.statement: The genus Coringasuchus was described by Alexander Kellner and colleagues in 2009.
facts.quote: Coringasuchus was described by Alexander Kellner and colleagues in 2009.

facts.statement: Fossils of Coringasuchus, including cranial material, were discovered in the early Cenomanian-age Upper Cretaceous Alcântara Formation on Cajual Island in northeastern Brazil.
facts.quote: It is known from fossils including cranial material discovered in rocks of the early Cenomanian-age Upper Cretaceous Alcântara Formation, Cajual Island, northeastern Brazil.

facts.statement: Coringasuchus lived during the Cenomanian stage, between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Coringasuchus belongs to the parent group Notosuchia.
Coringasuchus is classified within the class Reptilia.
